sentences.en: MIA: You know that joint presentation we've got to do this semester, Leo?
sentences.zh: MIA: 你知道我们这学期要做的那个联合报告吗，Leo？

sentences.en: LEO: On houses of the future?
sentences.zh: LEO: 关于未来住宅的？

sentences.en: MIA: That's right. I'm a bit concerned - are we meant to come up with creative new suggestions for these houses?
sentences.zh: MIA: 没错。我有点担心——我们是不是得为这些住宅提出富有创意的新建议？

sentences.en: LEO: I don't think so. It's more a matter of reporting and evaluating possible developments. But we mustn't be too general. we've got to support our points by referring to specific cases. So that'll need a lot of work.
sentences.zh: LEO: 我觉得没必要。这更多是关于汇报和评估可能的发展趋势。但我们不能太笼统，必须通过引用具体案例来支撑我们的观点。因此这需要大量工作。

sentences.en: MIA: I'm afraid so. When's it got to be done by?
sentences.zh: MIA: 恐怕确实如此。这个报告什么时候要交？

sentences.en: LEO: In about 6 weeks, so that's not too much of a rush.
sentences.zh: LEO: 大约六周后，所以时间上还不算太紧张。

sentences.en: MIA: Good. We'd better decide now what type of housing we're going to focus on.
sentences.zh: MIA: 太好了。我们最好现在就决定聚焦哪一类住宅。

sentences.en: LEO: How about housing for different generations living together?
sentences.zh: LEO: 共同居住的多代际住宅怎么样？

sentences.en: MIA: We could do. Or accommodation for one person?
sentences.zh: MIA: 我们也可以选这个。或者单人住所呢？

sentences.en: LEO: I think someone else is doing that. I was wondering about housing for the elderly? That's likely to become more important.
sentences.zh: LEO: 我觉得别人已经在做单人住所了。我在想老年人住宅如何？这方面的重要性可能会日益提升。

sentences.en: MIA: Yeah that's true. But I think your suggestion about intergenerational living might be more interesting - let's go with that.
sentences.zh: MIA: 是啊，的确如此。不过我觉得你提出的多代际共居方案可能更有趣——我们就选这个吧。

sentences.en: LEO: OK. Now I think the future demand is mainly going to be for accommodation in urban areas. So one way of meeting that demand might be to use existing commercial buildings and adapt them to form accommodation...
sentences.zh: LEO: 好的。我认为未来的主要需求将集中在城市地区的住宅上。因此，满足这一需求的一种方式可能是改造现有的商业建筑，使其转变为住宅……

sentences.en: MIA: ... or come up with original ways of organising space so that people can live in smaller homes. But I think the solution is to design multi-storey apartment blocks.
sentences.zh: MIA: ……或者创新性地规划空间，使人们能在更小的住宅中生活。但我认为解决方案是设计多层公寓楼。

sentences.en: LEO: Building up rather than out. yes.
sentences.zh: LEO: 向上建造而非向外扩展，没错。

sentences.en: MIA: Let's think of some specific developments for houses of the future.
sentences.zh: MIA: 我们来想想一些未来住宅的具体发展方案吧。

sentences.en: LEO: OK. How about increased use of roof space on high-rise buildings for gardens.
sentences.zh: LEO: 好的。比如在高层建筑屋顶上更多地开辟花园空间如何？

sentences.en: MIA: Yes. In fact it doesn't have to be high-rise, you can do it on a one-storey building in a suburb, but it would greatly improve how you feel if you live in an urban high-rise.
sentences.zh: MIA: 对。事实上，不一定非得是高层建筑，郊区的单层建筑也可以这么做；但若应用于城市高层住宅，则会极大改善住户的心理感受。

sentences.en: LEO: Especially if you don't have a balcony.
sentences.zh: LEO: 尤其是住户没有阳台的情况下。

sentences.en: MIA: Yes. I think homes of the future will all need access to a shared working space, somewhere in the same building or group of houses, where people can go and work instead of just having a laptop on the kitchen table.
sentences.zh: MIA: 是的。我认为未来的住宅都应配备共享工作空间——就在同一栋楼或同一住宅群内，供住户前往办公，而不只是把笔记本电脑放在厨房餐桌上。

sentences.en: LEO: Yes, so they aren't having to travel to an office but can still interact with others.
sentences.zh: LEO: 没错，这样他们就不必前往办公室通勤，却仍能与他人互动。

sentences.en: MIA: That's often how new ideas get generated - by chatting to someone from a different profession.
sentences.zh: MIA: 新想法往往就是这样产生的——通过与不同职业的人聊天。

sentences.en: LEO: Yeah. I read about a type of design where the internal walls of an apartment are moveable, so the space can be adapted over time as people's needs change.
sentences.zh: LEO: 是的。我读到过一种设计，公寓内部的墙壁是可以移动的，因此空间可以根据人们需求的变化而随时间调整。

sentences.en: MIA: Like when children leave school and start working but still continue to live with their parents for many years? Or when an elderly relative moves in with the family... it would mean they could still have their own space. specially designed for their needs.
sentences.zh: MIA: 比如孩子毕业开始工作后仍长期与父母同住？又或者年迈的亲戚搬来与家人同住……这样他们仍能拥有自己专属的空间，且该空间会特别根据他们的需求进行设计。

sentences.en: LEO: Yes. Have you heard about those smart bathroom mirrors which can monitor people's health? They recognise signs of illness and contact a doctor automatically?
sentences.zh: LEO: 是的。你听说过那种智能浴室镜子吗？它能监测人们的健康状况，识别疾病征兆并自动联系医生？

sentences.en: MIA: Hmm, not so sure they're a good idea.
sentences.zh: MIA: 嗯，我不太确定这是否是个好主意。

sentences.en: LEO: Nor am I. People might worry about conditions which aren't serious at all.
sentences.zh: LEO: 我也不这么认为。人们可能会为根本并不严重的健康状况而担忧。

sentences.en: MIA: What about transport? Wouldn't it be good if there were bike sheds with charging points, so people could store their electric bikes securely and charge them up at the same time.
sentences.zh: MIA: 那交通方面呢？如果自行车棚配备充电设施，人们就能安全存放电动自行车，同时为其充电，这难道不是很好吗？

sentences.en: LEO: Yes. That would encourage more people to cycle. instead of using their car.
sentences.zh: LEO: 是的。这将鼓励更多人骑自行车，而不是开车。

sentences.en: MIA: Much better for the planet.
sentences.zh: MIA: 对地球环境要友好得多。

sentences.en: LEO: I read about one housing development where cars had to be left just outside it, so the centre was all a pedestrianised area. Great for families with children.
sentences.zh: LEO: 我读到过一个住宅开发项目，要求汽车必须停放在小区外围，因此整个中心区域都是步行区。这对有孩子的家庭来说非常理想。

sentences.en: MIA: Maybe. But what if you're disabled or elderly. and can"t walk far? It wouldn't be so good for people like that.
sentences.zh: MIA: 或许吧。但如果有人残疾或年迈，无法长距离步行呢？对这类人群而言，这种设计就不太友好了。

sentences.en: LEO: No.
sentences.zh: LEO: 的确如此。

sentences.en: I saw a scheme for communal vegetable plots, where neighbours could decide what to grow together. That"d be a great way for older people to get to know one another, especially if they're no longer going out to work.
sentences.zh: 我看到过一个社区菜园计划，邻居们可以共同决定一起种植什么作物。这对老年人来说是彼此相识的好方式，尤其当他们已不再外出工作时。

sentences.en: Yes, doing something together's always more enjoyable, isn't it? Do you think...
sentences.zh: 是的，一起做事总是更愉快，不是吗？你觉得……
